mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined in 3 of the last 4 weeks (-39.9 to -40.9), indicating negative momentum. Autocorrelated mobility series tend to persist in direction over short horizons, so the downward trend should continue into the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -39.9 to -40.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, reversing the observed downward momentum.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility drops below -46.0 (a threshold suggesting active office-closure or stay-at-home guidance), reduced commuter-adjacent shopping and lunch-hour retail trips should compound, pulling RETAIL_REC further negative over the subsequent two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -46.0 for the current week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks despite WORKPLACES remaining below -46.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL (8.7 to 9.3) and decline in TRANSIT (-37.4 to -39.0) jointly signal a behavioral shift toward home-centered routines and reduced willingness to travel, which together suppress discretionary retail visits more than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose while TRANSIT fell over the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and TRANSIT stays depressed, breaking the joint co-movement link.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility dropped sharply from -0.3 to -3.4 in the most recent week, consistent with a seasonal transition (e.g., worsening weather) that reduces outdoor activity; this same seasonal driver should also depress outdoor-adjacent retail and recreation trips in the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -0.3 to -3.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week immediately following a PARKS drop of more than 2 points, indicating no shared seasonal driver.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has oscillated within a narrow band (-16.6 to -17.9) without a clear trend, suggesting essential-activity demand is stable; this stability implies no additional shock is propagating to broader retail categories, so RETAIL_REC should stabilize near its current level over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged only -16.6 to -17.9 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline for two more consecutive weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat, indicating decoupling of essential and discretionary retail.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility falls more than 2 points week-on-week (as it did from t-2w to t-0w, -38.6 to -39.0 cumulative with a larger single-week drop embedded), this signals active policy-driven restriction on public transit use, which mechanically limits access to retail districts and should drag RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -37.4 to -39.0 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks despite a TRANSIT drop exceeding 2 points, invalidating the transit-access mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen in each of the last four weeks (8.7 to 9.3), reflecting a persistent behavioral preference for staying home; this always-on sheltering tendency should directly translate into reduced retail and recreation visits within the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased monotonically from 8.7 to 9.3 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a continued RESIDENTIAL increase, contradicting the sheltering-behavior link.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of declining WORKPLACES and declining TRANSIT together indicates reduced overall out-of-home activity capacity (fewer commuters, less transit access), and this joint reduction amplifies the drag on RETAIL_REC beyond what either series predicts alone, with effects building over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT decline week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both declined from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or rises over the next two weeks even when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT decline concurrently, rejecting the amplification interaction.
